incident: warehouse chemical fire and plume, Conyers GA
soft_text: We are actively responding to an occurrence at our facility in Conyers, Georgia. Our employees are accounted for with no injuries reported. Our team is on the scene, working with first responders and local authorities to assess and contain the situation.
plain_text: A U.S. Department of Labor investigation found that improperly stored hazardous chemicals were the cause of a fire at a Company A facility. The investigation learned that the incident originated at a company warehouse that stored various chemicals. OSHA cited Company A for four serious and two other-than-serious violations and proposed $61,473 in penalties.
plain_neutral: Hazardous chemicals stored improperly were the cause of a fire at a Company A facility. The incident originated at a company warehouse that stored various chemicals.
contrast_text: Hazardous chemicals stored properly were not the cause of a fire at a Company A facility. The incident originated at a company warehouse that stored various chemicals.
notes: Soft text (Sept 30 2024, quoted in AJC via insurancejournal) names no fire, chemicals, cause or violations; plain text is OSHA April 7 2025 release trimmed (dropped 'The department's Occupational Safety and Health Administration'). Different dates, same incident; soft is early-response statement.

incident: corn dust explosion at grain mill, Cambria WI
soft_text: Company A is pleased that the CSB agrees that the tragic 2017 explosion that occurred at its Wisconsin mill was not started by fugitive dust relating to housekeeping procedures. Company A continues to hold those lost and injured in the accident in our hearts and joins with them, their loved ones, and our communities in the spirit of healing.
plain_text: The explosion occurred in May 2017, and fatally injured five employees and seriously injured another 14. The incident also ultimately destroyed the facility, resulting in over $15 million in property damage. The CSB determined the cause of the dust explosions and collapsed buildings was the ignition of combustible corn dust inside process equipment, which transitioned to multiple explosions.
plain_neutral: The explosion occurred in May 2017, and fatally injured five employees and seriously injured another 14. The incident also ultimately destroyed the facility, resulting in over $15 million in property damage. The cause of the dust explosions and collapsed buildings was the ignition of combustible corn dust inside process equipment.
contrast_text: The explosion occurred in May 2017, and no employees were injured. The incident also ultimately destroyed the facility, resulting in over $15 million in property damage. The cause of the dust explosions and collapsed buildings was the ignition of combustible corn dust inside process equipment.
facts: action: corn dust ignited in process equipment
notes: Soft = Dec 10 2023 company statement published by Chemical Processing (two sentences joined, 'its Cambria, Wisconsin mill' shortened to 'its Wisconsin mill'); soft says 'explosion' and 'accident' but gives no deaths count, no cause beyond rebuttal; names the explosion plainly, so only mildly euphemistic. Plain = CSB Dec 6 2023 release, three sentences trimmed.

incident: plant explosion and fire, four workers killed, Waukegan IL
soft_text: We are shocked and heartbroken by the tragedy that occurred in our plant last night. We have spent the day trying our best to support all of the members of our family as we attempt to process this terrible loss together. We want to express our extreme gratitude to all of the first responders who arrived at the scene.
plain_text: OSHA has cited Company A for 12 willful federal safety violations after four employees suffered fatal injuries in an explosion and fire at the company's plant on May 3, 2019. The company faces $1,591,176 in penalties. OSHA investigators determined Company A failed to ensure that electrical equipment and installations in the production area of the plant complied with OSHA electrical standards, and were approved for hazardous locations.
plain_neutral: Four employees suffered fatal injuries in an explosion and fire at the company's plant on May 3, 2019. Company A failed to ensure that electrical equipment and installations in the production area of the plant complied with OSHA electrical standards, and were approved for hazardous locations.
contrast_text: No employees were injured in an explosion and fire at the company's plant on May 3, 2019. Company A failed to ensure that electrical equipment and installations in the production area of the plant complied with OSHA electrical standards, and were approved for hazardous locations.
facts: action: failed to ensure electrical equipment approved for hazardous locations
